## Finding

`sdas8051` built from r17176 assembles the test case of the ticket and reports no error. In the
listing the second `.ORG`, the label `L1`, and the `LJMP` are at 008000. The reporter's listing
from SDCC 4.3.0 has FF808000 in these three lines, and the reporter's assembler reports a phase
error at `L1`. Neither was reproduced. The tests ran on a Linux host, the reporter's host is not
named in the ticket, and SDCC 4.3.0 was not built.

The object file from r17176 is wrong. The T line for the three branches begins with `FF FF 00`
where the address `00 00 00` belongs, and its R line has 18 bytes.

    T FF FF 00 60 00 00 00 20 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
    R 00 00 00 02 F1 07 04 00 00 F1 07 09 00 00 08 0C FF FF

For this file `sdld` warns of a byte PCR relocation error at offsets FFFF00 and FFFF05 and of a 2K
page relocation error at offset FFFF07. It then ends with a segmentation fault, which was not
examined.

## Cause

`outrwm` in `sdas/asxxsrc/asout.c` writes past the end of the relocation buffer `rel[]`, which has
16 bytes (`NREL`). In its branch for the 8051 and ds390 targets and an absolute destination, the
function calls `outchk(3, 0)`. The call asks for three free bytes in `txt[]` and for none in
`rel[]`. The function then writes four bytes to `rel[]` with `write_rmode` and `out_rw(0xFFFF)`.
In the test case 14 bytes of `rel[]` are in use after the `JZ` and `JB` lines, and `ACALL 0x0000`
writes bytes 15 to 18. `AJMP` uses the same code. `outr3bm`, which sdas390 uses for the two
instructions after `.amode 2`, has the same sequence with `outchk(4, 0)`.

What the two bytes after the buffer overwrite depends on the layout of the `sdas8051` binary. In
the binary built for this entry `txt[]` follows `rel[]`, so they replace the address at the start
of the T line. The reporter's result fits a binary in which `s_mask` follows `rel[]`. `rngchk` in
`sdas/asxxsrc/asexpr.c` returns FF808000 for 0x8000 when the low two bytes of `s_mask` are FF FF.
The reporter's binary was not examined. r14093, which set the version for the 4.3.0 release, has
the same `outchk` calls, the same buffer size, and the same `rngchk`.

## Fix

For an absolute destination, `outrwm` calls `outchk(3, 5)` and `outr3bm` calls `outchk(4, 5)`, and
`outchk` begins a new T line when fewer than five bytes of `rel[]` are free. The relocatable
branches of both functions, `outrxb`, `outrw`, and `outr3b` ask for five before they write a
relocation with `write_rmode` and `out_rw`, because `write_rmode` writes three bytes for a mode
above 0xFF. For `R_J11` and `R_J19` it writes two.

## Verification

`support/regression/tests/bug-3703.c` has an `acall 0x0123` after two instructions with a
relocation each and reads the two bytes of the `acall` from code memory. It checks the opcode
byte, so it needs the patch for local 0009. With that patch alone it fails for the six mcs51
variants (small, medium, large, huge, small-stack-auto, and large-stack-auto), and with both it
passes for them. On the host, stm8, and ucz80 the test has no assertion.

With both patches the ticket's file links without a message to `60 FE 20 00 F9 11 00` at address 0
and `02 80 00` at 0x8000. With these two patches and the one for bug #2970, the regression suite
for mcs51-small, stm8, and ucz80 and the diagnostics suite for mcs51 have no failure. `sdasstm8`
and `sdasz80` call neither function.

sdas390 is not in the builds that these suites use. It was built from the same source and run on
two files like the ticket's, one with `.DS80C390` in front, which uses `outrwm`, and one with
`.DS80C390` and `.amode 2`, which uses `outr3bm`. Without the patch for this ticket both T lines
begin with `FF FF 00`. With it the `ACALL` is in a T line of its own with the correct address.
The object files of sdas390 were not linked.

## Related

- The entry local 0009 describes the opcode byte 00 that r17176 writes for `ACALL` and `AJMP`. It
  is the last byte of the T line above.
- The entry local 0010 describes the `F9` in the bytes above. `sdld` computes the displacement of
  the `JB` as 2 too low, and `FB` is correct. The patch for this ticket leaves that as it is.
- The relocatable branch of `outrbm` in `asout.c` calls `outchk(1, 0)` and then writes a
  relocation with `write_rmode` and `out_rw`, which is the same defect. Only sdas6808 calls
  `outrbm`. It was not built, and `outrbm` is unchanged.
